title: Any client can read another company's orders
summary: GET /orders/{id} returns an Acme Traders order to a Bright Foods user.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1 and POST /api/orders with reference QA-rule-1 (item p-101, qty 1); note the id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id}
Observe HTTP 200 with the full order (see evidence for exact request)
expected: HTTP 403 or 404; companies never see each other's data
actual: HTTP 200 with the other company's order, items and totals
suspected_cause: Order detail handler does not compare the order's client_id with the caller's

regression_test.description: A Bright user GETs an Acme order id and expects 403/404

title: Clients can list all customer records, including personal data
summary: GET /admin/customers returns 200 with contact details, phone, national ID number and address to client roles; only admins should see it.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/admin/customers
Observe HTTP 200 and the full customer list (see evidence)
actual: HTTP 200 for acme-1, acme-2, bright-1 and zain-1 (role matrix in the admin-base run); response includes other companies' personal data
suspected_cause: Missing admin role check on the customers route (the sales report route has one)

regression_test.description: Each client role GETs /admin/customers and expects 403

title: Signing out does not end the session
summary: After POST /auth/logout returns success, the same token still works on GET /me.
steps: Sign in over the API as bright-1
POST /api/auth/logout
GET /api/me with the same token
Observe HTTP 200
suspected_cause: Logout does not revoke the token server-side

title: Tax is charged on the undiscounted subtotal
summary: For orders at or above 1,000.00 the 5% discount is applied but tax is calculated on the full subtotal, so customers are overcharged. The Client Portal confirmation shows the same wrong total.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 (API)
POST /api/orders with p-102 quantity 80 (subtotal 1,000.00)
Observe tax_cents 10000 and total_cents 105000
UI: Client Portal > New order, reference QA-ui-1, Ballpoint Pens x80, Place order; confirmation says Total: $1,050.00
actual: Tax 100.00, total 1,050.00. Also: 6,500.00 subtotal gives total 6,825.00 instead of 6,792.50; 1,012.50 gives 1,063.12 instead of 1,058.06
suspected_cause: Tax computed from subtotal instead of subtotal minus discount

regression_test.description: Orders of 79, 80 and 81 pens expect totals 1086.25, 1045.00 and 1058.06

title: Order validation accepts empty, zero, over-limit and fractional quantities
summary: POST /orders returns 201 for an empty items list, quantity 0, quantity 1001 and quantity 1.5, violating the stated rules and the OpenAPI spec.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
POST /api/orders with items [], then quantity 0, 1001, 1.5 (separate requests, see evidence)
Observe HTTP 201 each time
expected: HTTP 400: at least one item; quantity a whole number 1 to 1000

title: Server errors (HTTP 500) on odd order-list query values
summary: GET /orders returns 500 for page_size=0 and for q set to a single open parenthesis or a single backslash; page_size=-1 is accepted with 200 although the spec minimum is 1.
steps: Sign in over the API as acme-1
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 (also q=( and a lone backslash for q)
Observe HTTP 500
expected: HTTP 400 for invalid page_size; literal search for special characters
suspected_cause: Search text used unescaped as a regular expression; page size not range-checked

title: Malformed JSON returns a stack trace and server file paths
summary: Sending malformed JSON to POST /auth/login or POST /orders returns an error body containing a stack trace and server source paths.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with a malformed raw body
Observe HTTP 400 with a stack field and file paths (see evidence)
expected: A short error message with no internal details
actual: Stack trace and server paths in the response

regression_test.description: Malformed JSON expects 400 with no stack field

title: Submitting an order twice at once creates duplicate orders
summary: Two simultaneous identical POST /orders both succeed and create separate orders (My orders showed repeated QA-t80, QA-t81 and QA-t1000 rows). I am not sure whether the product intends to de-duplicate by reference.
steps: Sign in as acme-1
Send the same POST /api/orders twice in parallel
Observe two 201 responses with different ids
expected: One order, or the second refused
actual: Two orders created; the UI shows the same reference twice
suspected_cause: No idempotency or reference uniqueness check

regression_test.description: Parallel identical orders expect one order

title: Sales report is slow (about 4 seconds)
summary: GET /admin/reports/sales takes about 4 seconds; the Admin Portal Reports page stays empty meanwhile.
steps: Sign in as admin
GET /api/admin/reports/sales
Observe about 4003 ms

title: My orders on mobile: first row hidden under toolbar and Actions column clipped
summary: At 390px wide the first order row is partly covered by the filter toolbar and New order button, and the Total and View columns are cut off with no visible cue to scroll sideways.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Resize to 390x844
Open My orders
The first row is hidden behind the toolbar; Total is cut off and View is off-screen
expected: All rows and the View links reachable without hidden content
actual: Row covered; table scrolls sideways inside its box (456px inside 359px)
suspected_cause: Table wrapper overlaps the toolbar; no responsive layout

regression_test.description: At 390px no row is covered and View is reachable

title: Product dropdown on New order has no accessible label
summary: The product select has no label, so screen readers announce it by its first option.
steps: Sign in to the Client Portal as acme-1
Open New order
Run the page audit and look at unnamedControls
suspected_cause: Missing label or aria-label on the select

regression_test.description: Product select has an accessible name
